flags.description: Exports to the United States rose from 17% to 38% of silver exports between 2002 and 2003 (reported by PER to UN Comtrade).

Exports to China rose from 18% to 41% of zinc exports between 2008 and 2009 (reported by PER to UN Comtrade).
Documented commitments from China's institutions reached US$2.0 bn in 2010, 1% of GDP; the largest: Export-Import Bank of China (China Eximbank) (US$2.0 bn).

flags.description: Exports to China fell from 39% to 16% of zinc exports between 2015 and 2016 (reported by PER to UN Comtrade).
Exports to the United States fell from 26% to 5% of gold exports between 2018 and 2019 (reported by PER to UN Comtrade).
Documented commitments from China's institutions reached US$2.8 bn in 2020, 1% of GDP; the largest: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) (US$1.0 bn).

evidence.name: AidData Global Chinese Development Finance Dataset v3.0

flags.description: Exports to the United States fell from 50% to 30% of molybdenum exports between 2019 and 2020 (reported by PER to UN Comtrade).

sentences.text: In 2024, the influence index stands at 42.4 for China (band 33.4–58.1, from 3 of six components) and 8.8 for the United States (band 6.1–39.0, from 4 of six components). The net lean is +33.6 points toward China.
Over the five years to 2024, the index for China rose by 7.0 points and the index for the United States was broadly flat.

The value for China rests on trade export share, trade import share and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.

The value for the United States rests on trade export share, trade import share, finance flow and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.
In 2024, 48% of Peru's mineral exports (UN Comtrade value US$44.9 bn) went to China and 5.3% to the United States; together 53%, the rest to other destinations.
Since 2019 the share going to China rose by 3.9 points and the share going to the United States was broadly flat.
Relative to the 20-country export basket, its exports are specialised in phosphate potash (RCA 3.9), tin (RCA 2.0) and zinc (RCA 1.8).

7 sudden shifts in export shares are flagged from the customs data, the latest in 2020: Exports to the United States fell from 50% to 30% of molybdenum exports between 2019 and 2020 (reported by PER to UN Comtrade).

The DFC and EXIM records show US$157 m of documented commitments from US institutions to Peru over 2007–2026 (254 events).
Public and publicly guaranteed external debt owed to China was 0.0% of GDP in 2010 (World Bank IDS); no comparable series exists for debt owed to the United States.

The lenders with the largest recorded commitments to named recipients here are Export-Import Bank of China (China Eximbank) (US$2.6 bn), China Development Bank (CDB) (US$939 m) and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) (US$427 m).

sentences.text: In the UN General Assembly, voting agreement in 2024 was 77% with China and 41% with the United States.
Since 2019, agreement with China fell by 6.3 points and agreement with the United States rose by 14.9 points.
Too few mineral-related legislative records naming either actor have been scored for a stance series (five per year are needed); the text model is zero-shot baseline, not yet validated.

After Executive Order 13817: A Federal Strategy to Ensure Secure and Reliable Supplies of Critical Minerals (2017-12), the share of exports to China moved +8.6 points (34% before, 43% after); placebo p 0.21 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After Executive Order 14017: America's Supply Chains (100-day review including critical minerals) (2021-02), the share of exports to China moved +7.0 points (43% before, 50% after); placebo p 0.42 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After Section 301 tariffs on imports from China, first tranche in force (2018-07), the share of exports to China moved +6.5 points (37% before, 43% after); placebo p 0.37 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to China in 2030 is 61% (90% band 52%–69%), from random walk with drift partially pooled across countries (empirical Bayes), which beat naive persistence by 13% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to the United States in 2030 is 5.6% (90% band 0.0%–20%), from naive persistence, because no model beat it in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

The published forecast for the influence index of China in 2030 is 45.5 (90% band 25.3–63.2), from random walk with drift partially pooled across countries (empirical Bayes), which beat naive persistence by 1% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

The published forecast for the influence index of the United States in 2030 is 9.0 (90% band 5.2–13.0), from damped local linear trend (Kalman filter, maximum likelihood), which beat naive persistence by 2% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.
Under the stated scenarios the 2030 median share to China ranges from 49% (US sourcing rules bite) to 73% (accelerated China pull); these are what-ifs with a fixed yearly shift, not predictions.

In 2025, unavailable components: trade export share and trade import share (no reported trade for the year); legislative stance (no scored legislative records naming the actor); debt stock (no source for debt owed to the United States); finance flow (source coverage ends 2021); debt stock and diplomatic alignment (source coverage ends 2024).

Source coverage ends at different years: Chinese official finance to 2021, US finance to 2026, debt by creditor to 2024, UN votes to 2024 and trade to 2025; components beyond a source's coverage are unavailable, not zero.

Stance values come from the text model (zero-shot baseline, not yet validated); the rest of this brief rests on official statistics and the registered databases, each cited on its chart.

human.title: Peru: the warmest words to both powers, and half the copper to one of them
human.author: AI-drafted from the site's indicators; not yet reviewed by the project owner
human.text_md:
## Alignment

Peru's index leans toward China, 42.5 against 8.7 in 2024, the widest gap among the large exporters [index_value:influence:CN:2024] [index_value:influence:US:2024]. Of US$44.9 bn of mineral exports in 2024 (2025 is not yet reported), 48% went to China and 5.3% to the United States; copper is US$23.1 bn of the total and US$16.5 bn of it went to China, iron ore is almost entirely Chinese (US$1.7 bn of US$1.75 bn), and gold, US$13.6 bn, goes mostly elsewhere [concentration:share_cn_x:2024] [flow_trade:PER:copper:2024] [flow_trade:PER:iron_ore:2024]. The executives' coded statements are warm toward both powers, +0.83 toward the United States over six and +0.75 toward China over four, with no coded negative toward either, the clearest hedging balance in the dataset at 0.75 [statement:stance_us:PER:2024-2026] [statement:stance_cn:PER:2024-2026] [insights:hedging:PER]. US officials' statements about Peru are the most hostile toward China of any country, nine negatives of nine coded, and Chinese officials speak most about Peru, thirteen statements [statement:count:bloc=United States:PER] [statement:count:bloc=China:PER]. My reading: Peru is the contest's centre of gravity, and Lima's answer is to praise both.

## Trajectory

The Chinese share of exports rose from 13% in 2008 to 36% in 2016, 43% in 2020 and 48% in 2024 [concentration:share_cn_x:2016] [concentration:share_cn_x:2024]. Chinese commitments were US$4.8 bn over 2015–2021 after a US$7.2 bn peak in 2014, the Las Bambas year; US commitments were US$38 m and US$9 m in the two windows [flow_finance:CN:PER:2014] [flow_finance:US:PER:2015-2021] [flow_finance:US:PER:2022-2024]. Seven sudden trade shifts and three large commitments are flagged [anomaly_flag:sudden_trade_shift] [anomaly_flag:large_commitment]. Copper takes 72% of the mineral mentions and 52% of the export value, the closest match between talk and trade in the region [insights:talk_vs_trade_minerals:PER]. The window after the 2018 Section 301 tariffs shows the share to the United States falling 4.5 points, but the placebo value is 0.37, so it is no different from the series' other years [event_effect:us_section301_china_tranche1:US:window:PER]. The one coded press tone is positive toward the United States (+0.41 over nine 2026 headlines) [media_volume:tone_us:PER:2026].

## Risks and likely next moves

The models put China's share at 59% in 2030 at baseline, 71% under the China pull and 47% under US reshoring; the US share reaches 17% under reshoring [forecast:export_share:CN:baseline:2030:PER] [forecast:export_share:US:us_reshoring:2030:PER]. Parity would take US$9.6 bn of yearly exports switching, 4.1 times what the United States bought in 2024, and copper alone could cover it [insights:parity_gap:PER]. The Chancay port opened in November 2024 and the Section 232 copper tariff of 2025 exempts cathodes and concentrates [event:per_chancay_port_opening] [event:us_section232_copper]; in my reading the 2025 and 2026 copper rows will show whether the port deepened the Chinese share or merely shortened the voyage. The risk to the reading is the gold flow, which is large and goes to neither power.

## What would change this reading

A 2025 trade row showing the US copper share above 10%; a DFC or EXIM commitment to a Peruvian mine; or a second coder who read the executives' warmth toward China as weaker.

records.summary_en: At a business conference in Shanghai during her June 2024 state visit, Boluarte promoted Peru's mining potential, noting it holds eight of 17 critical minerals and that only 1.51% of its territory has been explored, and invited Chinese investors.
records.quote_original: I invite you to invest in Peru and be part of our development.
records.quote_en: I invite you to invest in Peru and be part of our development.
records.notes: Visit 23-28 Jun 2024; exact day of Shanghai speech not given; quote in English translation

speaker.name: Rómulo Mucho
speaker.role: Minister of Energy and Mines of Peru

records.event_context: Attack on Poderosa transmission towers; reactivating mining projects
records.summary_en: Mucho said some congressmen radically oppose progress and job creation, pledged to reactivate mining projects, review REINFO, and called for declaring mining formalization an emergency.
records.quote_original: existen congresistas que se oponen radicalmente al progreso, a la generación de puestos de trabajo
records.quote_en: there are congressmen who radically oppose progress, the creation of jobs

speaker.name: Laura Richardson
speaker.role: Commander, U.S. Southern Command

records.event_context: House Armed Services Committee posture hearing
records.summary_en: In testimony to the House Armed Services Committee, Richardson warned of the security risks of Chinese investments in South America, citing the Chancay megaport promoted by Beijing as a 'gateway from South America to Asia' among dual-use concerns.
records.quote_original: gateway from South America to Asia
records.quote_en: gateway from South America to Asia
records.notes: Port record; minerals relevance indirect (Chancay as mineral export hub). Quoted phrase is Beijing's characterization cited in her testimony

speaker.name: Mike Rogers
speaker.role: U.S. Representative (R-AL), Chairman, House Armed Services Committee

records.event_context: HASC hearing on national security challenges in North and South America
records.summary_en: Rogers said China's $3.6 billion port in Peru would be used to ship South American copper, lithium and other critical minerals to China for military modernization, and that CCP-backed companies own or operate mines and ports across the region.
records.quote_original: It will be used to ship South American copper, lithium, and other critical minerals to China to further their military modernization.
records.quote_en: It will be used to ship South American copper, lithium, and other critical minerals to China to further their military modernization.

speaker.name: Rómulo Mucho
speaker.role: Minister of Energy and Mines of Peru

records.event_context: Debate over REINFO and illegal mining
records.summary_en: Mucho said distortion of the REINFO formalization registry had enabled the expansion of illegal mining and that the registry needed review, excluding those not complying.
records.quote_original: Por la distorsión del Reinfo han aparecido muchos que están trabajando en eso.
records.quote_en: Because of the distortion of Reinfo, many have appeared who are working in that.

speaker.name: Song Yang
speaker.role: Chinese Ambassador to Peru

records.event_context: Interview with El Peruano on bilateral relations
records.related_entities: Puerto de Chancay; Chinese mining companies
records.summary_en: Song Yang said more than 10 Chinese mining companies had invested over US$23.1 billion in Peru, paying taxes and creating jobs, and presented Chancay port as a future integrated maritime hub for Latin America.
records.quote_original: Más de 10 empresas mineras chinas han invertido en el Perú, con una inversión total de más de 23.1 mil millones de dólares.
records.quote_en: More than 10 Chinese mining companies have invested in Peru, with total investment of over 23.1 billion dollars.
records.notes: El Peruano is the state gazette/newspaper

speaker.name: Margot Palacios
speaker.role: Congresswoman (Perú Libre)

records.event_context: Bill PL 2259 to nationalize copper exploitation
records.summary_en: Palacios filed bill 2259 to create a National Copper Corporation with exclusive rights over copper exploration, extraction and initial processing, including a state company to operate the MMG-controlled Las Bambas mine.
records.quote_original: crear una empresa nacional para operar la mina cuprífera Las Bambas
records.quote_en: create a national company to operate the Las Bambas copper mine
records.notes: Quote may be Forbes' paraphrase of the bill's objective

speaker.name: Aníbal Torres
speaker.role: President of the Council of Ministers of Peru

records.event_context: Dialogue with communities in Pumamarca, Apurímac; state of emergency over Las Bambas
records.summary_en: Torres told community members that the state of emergency in Challhuahuacho and Coyllurqui would be lifted only once they abandoned forceful actions against Las Bambas and engaged in peaceful dialogue.
records.quote_original: El estado de emergencia se levanta simultáneamente con el levantamiento de las actitudes de fuerza y restableciendo la paz social.
records.quote_en: The state of emergency is lifted simultaneously with the lifting of forceful actions and the restoration of social peace.

speaker.name: Baltazar Lantarón
speaker.role: Regional Governor of Apurímac

records.event_context: Las Bambas shutdown due to corridor blockade
records.summary_en: Lantarón criticized the Executive's negotiators as pusillanimous over the Las Bambas corridor blockade, warned of lost royalties and mining canon for Apurímac, and requested a 120-day emergency declaration on the southern mining corridor.
records.quote_original: la actitud pusilánime de los negociadores del Ejecutivo están generado nefastas consecuencias económicas
records.quote_en: the pusillanimous attitude of the Executive's negotiators is generating disastrous economic consequences

speaker.name: Mirtha Vásquez
speaker.role: President of the Council of Ministers of Peru

records.event_context: Chumbivilcas blockade halting Las Bambas
records.summary_en: With the Las Bambas road blockade past 20 days, Vásquez said the government was evaluating options including eviction of protesters and, as a last resort, a state of emergency in Chumbivilcas.
records.quote_original: Hay varias opciones que evaluar. No podemos permitir que se estén vulnerando ciertos derechos
records.quote_en: There are several options to evaluate. We cannot allow certain rights to be violated

speaker.name: Pedro Castillo
speaker.role: President of Peru

records.event_context: Controversy over PM Vásquez's announced closure of four mines in Ayacucho
records.summary_en: Amid market turmoil after the premier agreed with Ayacucho communities to close four mining operations, Castillo said there would be no unilateral or arbitrary decisions and reaffirmed his commitment to guarantee private investment including mining.
records.quote_original: No ha existido ni existirán decisiones unilaterales ni arbitrarias
records.quote_en: There have not been, nor will there be, unilateral or arbitrary decisions

speaker.name: Mirtha Vásquez
speaker.role: President of the Council of Ministers of Peru

records.event_context: Agreement with Ayacucho communities on mine closures
records.summary_en: Vásquez signed an agreement with Ayacucho communities confirming the closure of four mining operations and said mining expansions in the province would not be approved, prompting business backlash; a vice minister later said expansion plans could still be submitted.
records.notes: Agreement dated c. 19-20 Nov 2021; silver tag because affected mines (Hochschild) are gold-silver operations

speaker.name: Iván Merino
speaker.role: Minister of Energy and Mines of Peru

records.event_context: Three-week blockade of Las Bambas road in Chumbivilcas
records.summary_en: Merino partly blamed MMG's short-term decision to haul Las Bambas copper concentrate on a dirt road for unrest with communities, and proposed a train line as a longer-term solution.
records.quote_original: They made short-term decisions and that has a cost
records.quote_en: They made short-term decisions and that has a cost
records.notes: English wire translation

speaker.name: Pedro Francke
speaker.role: Minister of Economy and Finance of Peru

records.event_context: Proposed tax reform targeting mining windfall profits
records.summary_en: Francke argued that with copper above US$4/lb and costs around US$1/lb, the state should capture extraordinary mining profits and redistribute mining wealth through tax reform.
records.quote_original: Hay que redistribuir la riqueza, en particular la riqueza minera
records.quote_en: We must redistribute wealth, particularly mining wealth

speaker.name: Ana María Córdova
speaker.role: Legal representative of Perú Libre (Pedro Castillo campaign)

records.event_context: 2021 presidential runoff campaign
records.summary_en: Speaking for candidate Pedro Castillo, Córdova said the party would not expropriate or nationalize mines but would renegotiate contract conditions so the state and local populations get a bigger share of profits.
records.quote_original: Not to expropriate them, not to nationalize or anything, but so that the conditions in some way also favor populations where these industries or mining operations are involved
records.quote_en: Not to expropriate them, not to nationalize or anything, but so that the conditions in some way also favor populations where these industries or mining operations are involved
records.notes: English translation published by Bloomberg; original Spanish wording not seen

speaker.name: Francisco Sagasti
speaker.role: President of Peru (transitional)

records.event_context: Press conference with foreign media accredited in Peru
records.summary_en: Sagasti said his transitional government had no mandate to change economic direction and would ensure that foreign investments already under way, including in mining, continue, while arguing Peru should diversify beyond being a mining country.
records.quote_original: hará lo que hay que hacer para que continúen las inversiones extranjeras ya en proceso, ya sea en la minería o en otros sectores
records.quote_en: will do what must be done so that foreign investments already under way continue, whether in mining or other sectors
records.notes: Quote is in reported (third-person) form as published

speaker.name: Juan Carlos Liu
speaker.role: Minister of Energy and Mines of Peru

records.event_context: Mining Council review of Tía María license
records.related_entities: Tía María; Southern Copper; Consejo de Minería
records.summary_en: Liu said the Tía María license case was for the autonomous Mining Council to decide and that the government, following presidential guidelines, would abide by its ruling while promoting dialogue in the Tambo Valley.
records.quote_original: El caso de Tía María es un caso que está para la decisión de la Comisión de Minería.
records.quote_en: The Tía María case is one awaiting the decision of the Mining Commission.

speaker.name: Raúl Molina Martínez
speaker.role: Deputy Minister of Territorial Governance (PCM)

records.event_context: Chumbivilcas blockade of southern mining corridor used by Las Bambas
records.summary_en: The PCM vice minister urged Chumbivilcas communities to lift their blockade of the road used by Las Bambas to haul copper concentrate, stressing it is a public road and that demands must be legally viable.
records.quote_original: It is not possible to prevent the free movement of vehicles through the runway, including the miner's trucks, because it is a public road.
records.quote_en: It is not possible to prevent the free movement of vehicles through the runway, including the miner's trucks, because it is a public road.
records.notes: Quote is English wire translation; date is article date

speaker.name: Elmer Cáceres Llica
speaker.role: Regional Governor of Arequipa

records.event_context: Tía María license protests, Tambo Valley
records.summary_en: The Arequipa governor, backed by over 50 civil organizations, gave the central government 72 hours to declare the Tía María construction license null, while pursuing legal remedies and peaceful protests.
records.quote_original: Le daremos al Gobierno central 72 horas para que resuelva el tema de la licencia de construcción, o sea que declare su nulidad de oficio
records.quote_en: We will give the central government 72 hours to resolve the construction license issue, that is, to declare it null ex officio

speaker.name: Martín Vizcarra
speaker.role: President of Peru

records.event_context: Protests over Tía María construction license granted to Southern Peru (9 Jul 2019)
records.related_entities: Tía María; Southern Peru Copper; Grupo México
records.summary_en: Vizcarra said the construction license granted to Southern Peru for Tía María could not be annulled because the company had completed the administrative process, but called for dialogue and said construction would need proper conditions.
records.quote_original: No se puede anular, tenemos que conversar y fruto del diálogo, encontremos las soluciones y consensos
records.quote_en: It cannot be annulled; we have to talk, and through dialogue find solutions and consensus

speaker.name: Paola Bustamante
speaker.role: Minister of Development and Social Inclusion of Peru

records.event_context: Fuerabamba blockade of Las Bambas mining road; failed ministerial negotiation visit
records.summary_en: After protesters threw rocks at a government helicopter carrying a three-minister delegation to negotiate an end to a 51-day Fuerabamba community blockade of the Las Bambas copper mine road, Bustamante said the government would maintain its willingness to dialogue.
records.quote_original: We went with a disposition for dialogue and that's why we're going to continue with that disposition and see how things shape up tomorrow.
records.quote_en: We went with a disposition for dialogue and that's why we're going to continue with that disposition and see how things shape up tomorrow.
records.notes: Exact day not given (Wednesday before 29 Mar 2019, likely 27 Mar); quote is English wire translation of Spanish original

dataset_source.name: Political statements on critical minerals in Latin America (project dataset)
